newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION - Sympathy for the Pumas purrs in.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION - Sympathy for the Pumas purrs in.

text.p: NEW PLYMOUTH, June 24 - Sympathy for the wounded Pumas poured in from inside and outside of the country after their ruthless mauling by the All Blacks in the first rugby test, NZPA reports.
The sentiments, particularly from home, have given the touring Argentinians some motivation heading into the second and final test in Hamilton on Saturday night.

It was perhaps why the shocked team bounced right back from their 8-93 first test crushing at Athletic Park last Saturday, and were trying to adopt a single-minded approach to the second test in an effort to salvage some pride.
"You can't say they're bubbling, but they've got their heads up again and looking forward to making some amendments," the team's media liaison officer Frankie Deges said.
He said fans and followers of the game at home viewed their record loss with much sympathy.
Team members were pleasantly surprised to find messages of sympathy from New Zealanders as well.
"Everyone knows Argentina's passion for soccer. If the soccer team lost there'd be riots at home but they all know rugby is somewhat a minor sport yet," Deges said.
Former All Blacks coach Alex Wyllie, the tourists' technical adviser, said the team weren't feeling too down though they were shaken when the size of the loss did sink in.
"I think they've realised the enormity of the task ahead for the second test," he said.
Wyllie said he had no doubts the Pumas would have regrouped by Saturday to provide the All Blacks more resistance than they had a week earlier.
He indicated that up to three positions, particularly in the forwards, were under close scrutiny and changes in both the personnel and combinations were possible.
"They were just lost in the first test, don't know what happened there. What they should have been doing as a team they tried to do individually," Wyllie said.

One of the departments that concerned the Pumas team officials most was the back row of the scrum. Pablo Camerlinckx, Cristian Viez and Rolando Martin were anonymous, outclassed by the predatory skills of Josh Kronfeld and the defensive web set by Zinzan Brooke and Taine Randell.
Wyllie and his fellow Pumas selectors could consider one or two of Pablo Bouza, Miguel Ruiz and newcomer to the squad Raul Perez in their loose forward combination.
Perez replaced Carlos Lobbe in the touring side after the test flanker had an emergency appendicitis operation in Nelson last week.
Wyllie expected the second test side to be named tomorrow but a delay, as it happened before the first test, was possible.
